about: What the sessions changed on the site, newest first, in plain words for the owner's Admin page ('What changed lately'). Add with: python3 check-tools/admin.py change "<what>". Nothing private: both repositories are public.

changes.what: The autopilot's budget now grows with the profit of its sales and shrinks with its losses (a tick box under the budget, on by default), always within the practice money there is
A holding's trailing stop is now watched every half hour between check-ins, so a gain is not handed back while waiting up to 3 hours for the next check-in
Stock pages' news shows the right dates again (6,931 wrong date stamps corrected), and about 600 unchanged pages a day are no longer re-uploaded
On a phone the dashboard's market-data button is no longer hidden under the AI chat button, and the chat window fits small screens
Every sale is now looked at again a week and a month later, each against the S&P 500 over the same days, so the reviews can tell whether holding on would have paid
The Admin page's bill now shows your whole AWS bill first, then StockIQ's part of it (the one-off Cost Explorer charge included), then what running the site costs, service by service
Every share the autopilot buys now keeps its profit margin, debt and revenue growth, so the reviews can tell whether healthier companies do better (a measurement; it buys nothing differently)

The Admin page's AWS figure now shows what StockIQ itself costs to run ($0.48 this month, on course for about $0.80), with the one-off $2.65 Cost Explorer charge of 17 Oct and your other projects ($0.11) listed apart, so the red $3.24 is gone

Made for a laptop that is often off for days: stock news now looks back a week, stock pages keep their figures up to three weeks before leaving Google, and the first daily update after a gap catches up by itself.
A daily review by Claude now runs by itself every afternoon after the daily update: it checks the site and puts what it finds under Decisions for you; the next session acts on it.
The 'Answered' list now sits right under 'Decisions for you'; the contact page says StockIQ is a sole trader (it said Pty Ltd).

The 0-100 score on the stock pages and in the stock report was marking down shares that were rising, and on five years of prices it picked worse than chance. It now counts a strong rise and a price near the year's high for a share, as the screeners do (tested: better in 15 of 18 market-halves). Stock pages update with Monday's daily run.

Stock pages: 596 of the 958 in Google still showed 8 or 9 Oct figures, and would have started dropping out of Google this week. Prices now come through our own price function on AWS whenever Yahoo refuses this Mac; all 596 refreshed (online with Monday's daily run).
Reports no longer say 'real-time' (the site's prices can be delayed): they say 'latest available prices'.
Home page: the four index cards draw the day's real line (it was a fixed up or down shape) and no longer show January 2024 figures when the data fails.
Search: descriptions on nine pages that had none; the sign-in and unsubscribe pages kept out of Google; the four guides link to 32 stock pages.
Clean-up: three unused scripts and report writers removed (script.js, sidebar.js emptied, the old CoinSpot report).
The site is checked every night (site_audit.py): its findings are the Site check card below; it now also catches stale stock pages and made-up figures.
Admin page: Answered sits under Decisions for you; this list of changes added.
